english.title: Fail to protect girl from risk of genital mutilation
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were, at the relevant time, responsible for a girl under the age of 16 against whom a genital mutilation offence was committed
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 3A(1) and 5(2) of the Female Genital Mutilation Act 2003.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
person responsible, at the relevant time, for a girl under the age of 16
against whom a genital mutilation offence was committed

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Sections 3A(3) and (4) outline two cases in which a person would be deemed responsible for a girl for the purpose of this offence
(ii) Potential defences are listed in section 3A(5)
(iii) The relevant time means the time when the mutilation takes place
(iv) Genital mutilation offence means an offence under section 1, 2 or 3 of the Act

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6 / 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: maximum 7 years imprisonment and / or a fine

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 5(2)(b) of the Female Genital Mutilation Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time Limit For Prosecutions
None
